title.value: Genetic correlates of phenotypic heterogeneity in autism
title.justification: The title specifically states that the paper investigates the genetic aspects related to the phenotypic diversity within autism, focusing on genetic differences among autistic individuals.
title.quote: Genetic correlates of phenotypic heterogeneity in autism

extractions.description: This study examines the genetic factors contributing to the variation in core and associated features of autism among individuals. It uses genetic and phenotypic data from a large cohort to explore the genetic associations with these features, including the role of common and de novo genetic variants. The analyses aim to provide insights into how genetic diversity shapes cognition, behavior, and co-occurring conditions in autism.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on genetic studies related to autism, which revolve around genetic diversity, autism phenomenology, and gender differences rather than any direct climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: To address this gap, here we investigated genetic differences between autistic individuals... and identified six factors.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on any climate or ecological sustainable development theme, its primary focus is on genetic research related to autism, which does not fit any predefined categories related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: The substantial phenotypic heterogeneity in autism limits our understanding of its genetic etiology.

secondary_categories.justification: The topic remains consistent with genetic correlates in autism with no secondary connection to ecological or climate sustainability.
secondary_categories.quote: Deeper phenotypic characterization will be critical in determining how the complex underlying genetics shape cognition, behavior and co-occurring conditions in autism.

primary_sub_category.justification: As the primary category was not related to climate or ecological sustainability, the sub-categories are also not applicable in this context.
primary_sub_category.quote: We conducted a comprehensive factor analysis of core autism features in autistic individuals.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No sub-category related to ecological or climate sustainability matches the study's content, which is focused on autism genetics.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Autism Research Centre, Department of Psychiatry, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK.
